intro: In 1867 a baseball committee wrote that no club with a Black member could join its national body. In 1866 a London athletics club wrote that no mechanic, artisan or labourer could count as an amateur. Rules like these decided who could play long before anyone stepped onto a field. Some were printed in reports. Others were never written down at all, and owners simply kept them.

This unit studies those locks and the people who opened them. You will meet the Pythians of Philadelphia, Moses Fleetwood Walker, Rube Foster and Jackie Robinson. You will meet Jim Thorpe, John B. Kelly, Kathrine Switzer, Charlie Sifford and Althea Gibson. You will also visit Chicago's Comiskey Park, where the East-West All-Star Game began in 1933.

By the end, you will be able to name a rule, the people it shut out and the year it changed. You will be able to explain how a written rule differs from an unwritten agreement. You will also be able to show how shut-out athletes built their own leagues and associations.
bigQuestion: Who decided who was allowed to play, and how did the people shut out open the doors?

timeline.t: Amateur Athletic Club in London bars manual workers from amateur events
NABBP committee recommends keeping out clubs with Black members
Moses Fleetwood Walker plays for Toledo in the American Association
International League votes to approve no new contracts with Black players
Northern rugby clubs meet in Huddersfield and form their own union
Jim Thorpe's 1912 Olympic medals are taken away
Negro National League founded at the Paseo YMCA in Kansas City
First East-West All-Star Game at Comiskey Park, Chicago
Jackie Robinson plays for the Brooklyn Dodgers on April 15
PGA of America removes its Caucasian-only clause
Boston Marathon officially opens to women
MLB counts seven Negro leagues of 1920–1948 as major leagues

words.d: the barrier that kept Black players off white professional teams from the late 1880s until 1947
an unwritten promise kept without signing anything
keeping a person or group out
the Black professional baseball league founded in Kansas City in 1920
traveling from town to town to play games without a league schedule
opening a group or place to people who had been kept out
the official with power over a whole sport
an athlete who has not been paid for sport
a rule that barred manual workers from amateur competition
money paid to replace wages a player lost while playing
the rules about who may enter or play
the PGA rule, from 1934 to 1961, that limited membership to white golfers

test.q: What did the NABBP nominating committee recommend in 1867?
choices: keeping out any club with a Black member
test.why: The December 1867 report put the exclusion of Black clubs in writing.

test.q: How was the major league color line kept from the late 1880s to 1947?
choices: through a law passed by Congress
through a rule in the National League constitution
through an unwritten gentlemen's agreement among owners
test.why: No written major league rule has been found; owners simply did not sign Black players.

test.q: Who is recognized as the first openly Black major league player?
test.why: Walker played for Toledo of the American Association in 1884.

test.q: Who led the founding of the Negro National League in 1920?
test.why: Foster, owner of the Chicago American Giants, led the Kansas City meeting.

test.q: Where was the East-West All-Star Game first played?
test.why: The Negro leagues' all-star game began at Comiskey Park in September 1933.

test.q: Which date marks Jackie Robinson's first game for Brooklyn?
test.why: Robinson played first base for the Dodgers on April 15, 1947.

test.q: Which major league team was the last to field a Black player?
test.why: Pumpsie Green joined the Red Sox in July 1959.

test.q: What did the mechanics clause do?
choices: barred manual workers from amateur events
set the length of the marathon
test.why: The 1866 rule shut out any mechanic, artisan or labourer.

test.q: What was the argument behind the 1895 rugby split?
choices: whether rugby should join the Olympics
whether clubs could pay broken time to working players
whether matches could be played on Sunday
test.why: Northern clubs wanted broken-time pay; the Rugby Football Union refused.

test.q: Why did Jim Thorpe lose his Olympic medals in 1913?
choices: he had worked as a bricklayer
he appeared in a ski advertisement
he had been paid to play minor league baseball
test.why: Pay for baseball in 1909–1910 broke the amateur rules of the time.

test.q: Which statement about Avery Brundage is correct?
choices: as IOC president from 1952 to 1972 he enforced strict amateur rules
test.why: Brundage led the IOC for twenty years and pushed to bar athletes who took money.

test.q: When did women first compete in the modern Olympic Games?
test.why: Women first competed in Paris in 1900; Charlotte Cooper won tennis singles.

test.q: What did Kathrine Switzer do in 1967?
choices: won the first Olympic women's marathon
ran the Boston Marathon with an official number
test.why: Switzer entered as "K. V. Switzer" and finished the race despite an official's attempt to stop her.

test.q: How did shut-out athletes respond in tennis and baseball?
choices: they joined the Rugby Football Union
they moved every game to Europe
they built their own bodies, such as the ATA and the Negro National League
test.why: The American Tennis Association (1916) and the Negro National League (1920) were built by Black athletes and owners.

test.q: What did Major League Baseball decide in 2020?
choices: to count seven Negro leagues of 1920–1948 as major leagues
to open the Hall of Fame
test.why: MLB announced the change on December 16, 2020, and added the statistics in 2024.

write.prompt: Was a written rule or an unwritten agreement harder to overturn? Argue from the unit's records. Compare the 1867 NABBP committee report or the PGA's 1934 clause with the major leagues' unwritten color line. Name each document or event, its date and the people it shut out.
tips: Name each rule, agreement or record, with its year.
Write the rule first, then the people it shut out, then the year it changed.
Use unit terms such as exclusion, gentlemen's agreement and integration.
Include what the shut-out athletes built or did, not only what was done to them.
Compare the cases; do not just list them.
